reason: All five requirements are implemented against real SQLite with real file-backed databases and verified by an independent reader. Two genuine defects were found and fixed: a Windows file-locking failure in restore, and the discovery that PRAGMA integrity_check alone does not detect a byte flip in a SQLite free page, which is why digest verification was added.
real_vulnerabilities_found: Restore could not replace a live database on Windows because the process held a lock on its own file; fixed by disposing the connection before the swap and rolling back on failure
PRAGMA integrity_check tolerates corruption in unused pages, so a corrupted backup could have restored silently altered data; fixed with digest verification via restore_verified
known_limitations: Backup encryption is reported via the manifest 'encrypted' flag but no encryption is applied in this node; REQ-033 treats encryption as optional and this is recorded as outstanding rather than claimed
Concurrency is proven at thread level against a single SQLite file; multi-machine concurrency is out of scope for a local-first desktop application (ADR-003)
